feature_contracts.scope: static interface binding; behavioral results are verified separately

requirements.requirement: Expose a firmware-visible CSR/MMIO control and status interface.
Emit bounded host request traffic and accept bounded host response traffic.
Validate response status, sequence, and age before enabling command shaping.
Provide deterministic command packing and saturation for active aerodynamic surfaces.
Aggregate and report latched/live faults and software logging fields.
Inhibit actuator validity on reset, faults, stale data, timeouts, or not-armed conditions.
The MMIO interface shall be real and decode all declared registers through RTL.
host_req_valid shall remain asserted until host_req_ready is observed or timeout aborts the request.
host_rsp_ready shall follow the transaction state and shall not create unbounded combinational paths.
Responses with mismatched sequence, invalid status, or expired age shall be rejected and shall not update command outputs.
When a valid response is accepted, the packed actuator command shall be clamped to configured min/max limits.
Faults shall be latched until explicitly cleared by software under safe conditions.
No fallback command substitution, fallback register, or fallback status bit shall be created; invalid conditions only inhibit command validity.

On reset, clear pending requests and latched state, deassert host_req_valid and cmd_valid, drive aero_cmd_out to a deterministic inhibited value, clear fault flags to a deterministic reset value, and initialize sequence and age counters to zero. No actuator command is asserted valid on reset.
Decode 64-bit MMIO writes into explicit semantic control outputs.
Return 64-bit MMIO readback words for status and configuration.
Expose live status and fault summary inputs to firmware through readback.
Provide semantic request metadata outputs for transport composition.
Ensure every declared register is reachable through RTL decode.
Every register defined in register_contract shall be directly decodable and readable.
Writable control fields are semantic outputs and shall be explicitly connected to downstream modules.
RO live/status fields are semantic inputs and shall not be modeled as writable storage in the MMIO block.
The MMIO block shall not expose inaccessible internal state as software-visible registers.

On reset, drive all writable control outputs to zero and drive deterministic safe defaults for timeout and clamp registers as implemented by the top-level integration contract. ctrl_rdata shall return a deterministic reset value. ctrl_ready shall indicate an idle-ready state. No live status is asserted by the register block on reset.
Maintain request valid until host_req_ready or local timeout abort.
Track expected and last-seen sequence numbers.
Qualify response availability and report transaction faults.
Provide the transport-side last sequence and fault summary for software readback.
host_req_valid shall persist until accepted or timeout-aborted.
host_req_data shall encode only compact metadata and shall not carry bulk tensors, geometry arrays, or flow fields.
host_rsp_ready shall be asserted only when the transaction is armed and a response is expected by state.
Responses with mismatched sequence or inactive transaction state shall not be promoted to tx_response_valid.
Age counting shall be bounded and deterministic.
Fault codes shall identify timeout, stale-data, invalid-response, and not-armed/not-enabled conditions in a compact encoding.

On reset, deassert host_req_valid and host_rsp_ready, clear transaction active state, clear request-issued indication, zero expected sequence, age, and last-sequence tracking, and clear latched transport faults to a deterministic reset value. No request remains pending across reset.
Verify response sequence and transaction state alignment.
Check response status codes and reject invalid status values.
Clamp the candidate output target to configured min/max limits.
Forward only validated target, rate-limit, and mode fields to command shaping.
Generate explicit validation fault indicators for status and software recovery.
Only matching, active, non-expired responses may be marked valid.
Out-of-range target values shall be clamped before command shaping.
Invalid status codes shall force rejection and fault reporting.
Not-armed or not-enabled conditions shall prevent response acceptance and produce explicit rejection indication.
The block shall not silently substitute any alternate command; it only qualifies or rejects the response.
On reset, deassert valid_response, clear validation fault outputs, and drive validated fields to deterministic safe values with no claim of a valid actuator update.
Pack the final actuator command word in a deterministic format.
Apply saturation to the validated target using configured limits.
Propagate validated rate-limit and mode bits into the packed command encoding.
Provide explicit command-valid indication only for accepted responses.
The command word shall be deterministic and compact.
The command word shall include at least target/deflection, optional rate-limit, and mode bits.
Saturation shall prevent out-of-range actuator values from propagating.
No command substitution is generated; absence of validation results in command invalidation only.
On reset, deassert cmd_valid and drive aero_cmd_out and the saturated field outputs to deterministic inhibited values. No active actuator command is asserted on reset.
Aggregate validation and transport faults into compact live and latched status.
Encode a deterministic fault_out summary word.
Expose last accepted sequence and response age for software logging.
Hold faults latched until explicitly cleared under safe conditions.
Report busy and valid-response status for observability.
Faults shall remain latched until clear_faults is written and the system is not in an active fault-triggering condition.
Status outputs shall indicate inhibited operation due to not-armed, stale, timeout, or invalid conditions rather than command substitution.
No automatic silent recovery is permitted without explicit software action or a valid new request/response cycle.
The status block shall not drive any transport or command behavior directly; it only reports and aggregates state.

On reset, clear latched faults to a deterministic value, deassert busy and valid-response indicators, clear stale/timeout/invalid status bits, and initialize last sequence, last fault code, and response age to zero. fault_out shall be driven to a deterministic reset encoding.
